why: the capture table carries three kinds alike in the lint and the interpreter: a hook result whose method is a request (another path at the click is a WITNESS; two pure render consts in another order prove, the held handler keyed by the hook and the method), a ref cell read as a cell (another initial value is another content, a WITNESS through the held handler's key), and a prop read through a nested binding (a fired setter over a ref cell and a nested prop is interpreted, every fire agreeing); a ref cell write inside a held function is a cell step (no re-render): lane A keeps the writing handler as a function value keyed by its text and captures, so a dropped write and two writes in another order are not proved, while lane B's interpreter steps the cells and the second click witnesses the dropped write; two writes in another order leave the same cells (PASS-bounded, every fire agreeing); a render-time write stays refused (escape handler_capture_unknown, renderWrite)
